summary: A titled list of uniform rows from data: each row a title, an optional subtitle, a value, a leading mark, a trailing control and optional details to tap open. It adapts by itself to any window: rows while tall, subtitles and the header gone when short, as many rows as fit at 48 dp, two or three columns when wide, an empty state when the app sends no rows.

rows.doc: One array per row, by position: [title, subtitle, value, lead, trail, details, onClick, detailsNode, label]. Stop at the last field you use and put null for one you skip. title, subtitle, value and details are a text, a "@textVariable" or a text object (textFromFloat, textMerge); lead, trail and detailsNode are any node (Icon, Badge, Switch, Slider, canvas). This list is also the capacity: the app changes the strings and count, not the number of rows written

title.doc: Heading, one line, dropped when short. Omit for no header

count.doc: How many rows to show, a number or "@variable" the app sets. 0 shows the empty state. Default: all of rows

maxRows.doc: Write at most this many of rows

surface.doc: divided: a rule between rows. card: each row a rounded surface. none: bare rows

density.doc: compact: 40 dp minimum rows and smaller text, for small widgets only (below the touch guideline)

rowHeight.doc: The tallest a row grows to share spare height: 72 by default (compact 56). The minimum stays 48 (compact 40). Give 48 for rows that never grow

maxColumns.doc: Most columns when wide; 1 for a list that never becomes a grid

tileWidth.doc: Width in dp each column needs: columns = width / tileWidth, up to maxColumns

summaryHeight.doc: Height of the summary slot when it sits above the rows

summaryAt.doc: Window height from which the summary shows above the rows; below, it goes, unless the window is wide enough to put it beside them

sideAt.doc: Width from which the summary sits beside the rows instead of above

detailsHeight.doc: Height of an open row's details, space included (two lines of text by default). The list reserves it when a row opens. Taller detail nodes need a larger value

open.doc: Which row is open, from 1; 0 none. Bind it to read or preset it

trailWidth.doc: Share of the row's width for the trailing cell, 0 to 1 (0.5): needed for a Slider, which fills what it is given. Left out, the cell wraps its content (a Switch, a Badge)

valueSize.doc: Value size in sp; default the title's. Larger makes a number the row's hero

embedded.doc: true: no background and no outer padding, for a list inside your own screen. Then pass width and height

width.doc: The width the list has. Only when it is not the whole window

height.doc: The height the list has. Only when it is not the whole window

summary.doc: A line or block about the whole list ("4 of 6 up", a total, a bar). Above the rows when tall, beside them when wide, gone when short

headerEnd.doc: At the end of the header line: a Badge, an IconButton

empty.doc: Replaces emptyText in the empty state: an icon and a sentence

pitfalls: rows is positional, because a list item's fields cannot be named in a body ($each has no @r.title): [title, subtitle, value, lead, trail, details, onClick, detailsNode, label]. Stop at the last field used; null skips one

Rows from the app: put "@name1" in the fields, declare the strings as exported root variables (with distinct initial values, or they share one text id) and give count: "@n". rows is the capacity: the app can show fewer rows, never more than were written, and each written row costs about 300 B to 1 KB in the document (expand mode, because of text)

A row is tappable only if it has details or onClick, that is 6 fields or more. Its label is built live from its title, subtitle and value (textMerge, so host text is read as it is now); a 9th field replaces it. Say a status that only an icon shows with that field. Rows without a tap are read text by text and a trailing Switch or Slider is its own target with its own label: give it one
To make a whole row flip a switch, give the row onClick and show the state with a lead or a trailing drawing without its own tap: a Switch inside a tappable row is two targets

All decisions read the window (or width and height when you pass them) and the row count, never the content: long text ellipsizes and never changes the layout. Below 180 dp of cell width the chevron goes, and the lead too when the row also has a value or a wide trailing control, so the title stays readable. If the lead is a status, say it in the title or label as well

A list cut to fit says "3 of 8" in the header. Where the header is dropped to fit one more row (a short window), nothing says rows are missing. Set maxRows, or keep the window at 200 dp or more, when that matters
Details have a fixed height (detailsHeight, 40 dp: two lines of text): a taller detailsNode is cut off unless you raise it. In a short window the rows slide so the open one stays on screen
A value is at most 42 % of the row and ellipsizes; the title takes the rest. A long value is a sign it belongs in the subtitle
embedded: true for a list inside a screen. Pass width and height of the box it gets: the layout cannot read its parent's size in a visibility, so the window is the default
surface card in mono is a 1 dp ring. The row is laid out by a flow with exact cell widths: a surface or padding of your own around it needs width passed
